title: Flat scheme patching over an infinitesimal pushout
statement: Let $T\to T^+$ be a thickening of schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $T\to S$ be an affine scheme morphism (inverse images of affine opens are affine). Put $P=S\amalg_T T^+$, the scheme pushout [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout]. For schemes $X/S$, $Y/T^+$ and an isomorphism $X\times_S T\simeq Y\times_{T^+}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], set $U=X\times_S T$ and $Z=X\amalg_U Y$, again the scheme pushout. Then $Z\to P$ is flat and locally of finite presentation if and only if both $X\to S$ and $Y\to T^+$ are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Moreover for every scheme $W\to P$ which is flat, without any finite-presentation hypothesis, the canonical map $$(W\times_P S)\amalg_{W\times_P T}(W\times_P T^+)\longrightarrow W$$ is an isomorphism. These assertions allow arbitrary thickenings, without a finite-order or Noetherian hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts] to the given triple. In particular $X=Z\times_P S$ and $Y=Z\times_P T^+$. For each affine pair $Z_0\to P_0$ use its notation $R=B\times_A A'$ and $E=D\times_C C'$, with $C=D\otimes_B A=C'/IC'$. These are charts of the actual morphisms, with their structural ring maps; no flatness has yet been assumed.

Assume $X\to S$ and $Y\to T^+$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. On every pair of charts from Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] give that $B\to D$ and $A'\to C'$ are flat and finitely presented. The isomorphism $D\otimes_B A\simeq C'/IC'$ is exactly the compatibility needed by [lem-sfb-fibre-product-algebra-flat-presentation]; its finite-presentation assertion gives that $R\to E$ is flat and finitely presented. This holds for every affine pair $Z_0\to P_0$, so the affine flatness criterion proves $Z\to P$ flat. Every point has such affine neighbourhoods, and their finite presentations give local finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

Conversely suppose $Z\to P$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. By Step 1 the two component maps are base changes; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] proves both flat. For every affine pair $Z_0\to P_0$, [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] makes $R\to E$ finitely presented. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition], the maps $B\to E\otimes_R B$ and $A'\to E\otimes_R A'$ are finitely presented. Step 1 identifies these target algebras with $D,C'$. The inverse-image charts $X_0,Y_0$ cover $X,Y$ as $Z_0,P_0$ vary (choose affine neighbourhoods of each image point). Thus they give the finite presentations required at every point by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

Let $W\to P$ be flat and let $\epsilon:H=(W\times_P S)\amalg_{W\times_P T}(W\times_P T^+)\to W$ be the canonical map. Cover $W$ by affine opens $W_0=\operatorname{Spec}L$ lying over affine $P_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Step 1 applied to the base pushout (take $X=S,Y=T^+$) gives affine $S_0,T^+_0,T_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the three restrictions over $W_0$ have coordinate rings $L\otimes_R B,L\otimes_R A',L\otimes_R A$. The middle closed-immersion ring map is surjective, being the quotient by $I$. By open locality in [lem-sfb-infinitesimal-pushout-affine-charts] and [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout], $\epsilon^{-1}(W_0)$ is the spectrum of their ring fibre product. Flatness of $L$ over $R$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. The final assertion of [lem-sfb-fibre-product-algebra-flat-presentation] identifies the ring map of $\epsilon$ on this open with an isomorphism. Its inverse gives a local inverse to $\epsilon$; on overlaps two such inverses agree after restricting to an affine cover, since both invert the same restricted isomorphism. They glue by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to a two-sided inverse. Only flatness of $L$, not finite presentation, was used; $I$ need only be nil for the scheme pushout charts, and nowhere is a uniform nilpotence exponent required.

lean.statement: theorem scheme_pushout_flat_patching {T T' S P : Scheme.{u}} (i : T ⟶ T') (a : T ⟶ S) (hi : IsThickening i) [IsAffineHom a] (j : S ⟶ P) (b : T' ⟶ P) (hp : IsPushout a i j b) : (∀ {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ T') (e : pullback f a ≅ pullback g i) (he : e.hom ≫ pullback.snd g i = pullback.snd f a) (l : X ⟶ Z) (r : Y ⟶ Z) (hz : IsPushout (pullback.fst f a) (e.hom ≫ pullback.fst g i) l r), (Flat (SchemePushoutPatching.structureMap hp f g e he hz) ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation (SchemePushoutPatching.structureMap hp f g e he hz)) ↔ (Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f) ∧ (Flat g ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation g)) ∧ (∀ (W : Scheme.{u}) (w : W ⟶ P), Flat w → ∃ (H : Scheme.{u}) (l : pullback w j ⟶ H) (r : pullback w b ⟶ H) (hh : IsPushout (SchemePushoutPatching.baseChangeLeft a j w) (SchemePushoutPatching.baseChangeRight hp w) l r), IsIso (hh.desc (pullback.fst w j) (pullback.fst w b) (by simp [SchemePushoutPatching.baseChangeLeft, SchemePushoutPatching.baseChangeRight])))
lean.note: The isomorphism e is over T, rendered by he. Pushout representatives are specified by IsPushout. The flat-W clause supplies its pushout and states that its canonical desc to W is an isomorphism; this is independent of the representative by uniqueness of pushouts.
